title: Fixed-residue Artinian lifting tests adic formal smoothness
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $k$ be a finite extension of $R/\mathfrak m_R$ [def-weil-field]. A local ring here has exactly one maximal ideal. Let $(C,\mathfrak m_C)$ be a complete Noetherian local $R$-algebra, with local structure map and a specified $R$-algebra identification $C/\mathfrak m_C\cong k$; completeness is for the maximal-ideal-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $\mathcal C_{R,k}$ have as objects Artinian local commutative $R$-algebras with specified $R$-algebra identification of their residue field with $k$, and as morphisms local $R$-algebra maps inducing the identity on $k$. Artinian means every descending chain of ideals stabilizes. For $A\in\mathcal C_{R,k}$ let $h_C(A)=\operatorname{Hom}_{R,\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{cont}}(C,A)$ be the set of local $R$-algebra maps $C\to A$ inducing the identity on $k$ under the specified identifications and continuous, where continuity means that the map kills $\mathfrak m_C^n$ for some $n\geq1$. Then $R\to C$ is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] if and only if, for every surjection $p:A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ in $\mathcal C_{R,k}$ and every $u\in h_C(A)$, there exists $u'\in h_C(A')$ with $p\circ u'=u$.

source.place: Tag 0DYL, lemma-smooth, equivalence (1) and (2), and its proof; the converse uses More on Algebra, Tag 0DYG (more-algebra.tex, lemma-fs-local), equivalence with small-extension tests. The category is Tag 06GC, definition-CLambda.

proof.text: Assume $R\to C$ is formally smooth for $\mathfrak m_C$. Let $p:A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ and $u\in h_C(A)$ be given, and put $I=\ker p$. Since $p$ respects residue fields, $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_{A'}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent], choose $N\geq1$ with $\mathfrak m_{A'}^N=0$; thus $I^N=0$. Identify $A'/I$ with $A$. For $1\leq j<N$, the quotient map $A'/I^{j+1}\to A'/I^j$ has square-zero kernel: $I^{2j}\subseteq I^{j+1}$. These quotients are local with the same residue field as $A'$: an element invertible modulo a nilpotent ideal is invertible, since $1-z$ has inverse $1+z+\cdots+z^{N-1}$ when $z^N=0$.

source.place: Tag 0DYL, lemma-smooth, forward direction; nilpotence input Algebra Tag 00J8, lemma-artinian-radical-nilpotent

proof.text: Starting with $u_1=u:C\to A'/I$, lift inductively through $A'/I^{j+1}\to A'/I^j$ using [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. If $u_j$ kills $\mathfrak m_C^t$, every algebra lift $u_{j+1}$ sends $\mathfrak m_C^t$ into the square-zero kernel and therefore kills $\mathfrak m_C^{2t}$. The induced residue map of a lift is the residue map of $u_j$, since the quotient induces a residue-field isomorphism. It is consequently the prescribed identity on $k$. Its inverse image of the maximal ideal is $\mathfrak m_C$, because this residue map is an isomorphism, so the lift is local as well as continuous. The base case has these properties by definition of $h_C$. At $j=N$ this gives $u_N:C\to A'$ with $pu_N=u$, as required. If $N=1$, $p$ is already an isomorphism and its inverse composed with $u$ gives the lift.

source.place: Tag 0DYL, lemma-smooth, forward direction, expanding the square-zero lifting definition

proof.text: Conversely assume the lifting property for $h_C$. Consider any small extension $B'\twoheadrightarrow B$, local map $R\to B'$, and local $R$-algebra map $g:C\to B$ inducing a residue isomorphism, as in [lem-sfb-local-square-zero-small-extension-reduction] with $S=C$. Write $\alpha:C/\mathfrak m_C\to k$ for the given identification and $\bar g:C/\mathfrak m_C\to B/\mathfrak m_B$. Give $B$ the residue identification $\alpha\bar g^{-1}$ and $B'$ the one obtained by composing this with the quotient-induced residue isomorphism. They are $R$-algebra identifications; all maps now respect $k$. Since $g$ is local and $\mathfrak m_B$ is nilpotent by [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent], $g$ kills a power of $\mathfrak m_C$, so $g\in h_C(B)$. The hypothesis supplies its lift. This verifies every small-extension test in the reduction lemma. Apply that lemma: $C$ is Noetherian and $R\to C$ is local. We obtain lifts for every local square-zero test ring with nilpotent maximal ideal and residue isomorphism, including non-Artinian test rings.

source.place: Tag 0DYL, lemma-smooth, converse; Tag 0DYG, lemma-fs-local, (3) implies (2)

proof.text: To verify [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic], take any $R$-algebra $D$, ideal $J$ with $J^2=0$, and $g:C\to D/J$ killing $\mathfrak m_C^t$, $t\geq1$. Put $T=g(C)$ and let $E\subseteq D$ be the inverse image of $T$. It is an $R$-subalgebra containing $J$, and $E/J=T$. Since $\ker g$ contains $\mathfrak m_C^t$ and is proper, it is contained in $\mathfrak m_C$: anything outside the latter is a unit and cannot belong to a proper ideal. Thus $T=C/\ker g$ is local, with maximal ideal $g(\mathfrak m_C)$, its $t$th power zero, and residue field $C/\mathfrak m_C$. The inverse image $M$ of this maximal ideal in $E$ satisfies $M^t\subseteq J$ and $M^{2t}=0$, and $E/M$ is that same residue field. Every element outside $M$ is invertible: lift an inverse in $T$ and correct the product $1+j$ using $(1+j)^{-1}=1-j$, since $j^2=0$. Thus $E$ is local with maximal ideal $M$. The maps $R\to E$ and $C\to E/J$ are local, as is seen on their residue fields; $C\to E/J$ induces a residue isomorphism. Apply the local square-zero lifting property obtained in step 3 to $E,J$. Compose the resulting lift $C\to E$ with $E\hookrightarrow D$. This lifts $g$ in the arbitrary diagram. If $D/J$ is the zero ring, $J=D$ and $J^2=0$ force $D=0$, and the unique map is a lift. This proves adic formal smoothness and finishes the converse.
